CT4104 overview

CT4104 Topic Guide

Security foundations

Choose a control only after identifying the security property and asset it must protect.

Rapid exam refresher

  • CIA separates secrecy, tamper detection and availability.
  • authentication identifies, authorisation permits.
  • threat/vulnerability/control and residual risk differ.
  • cue: map property to control.

Purpose, scope and examiner demand

Confidentiality, integrity and authentication provide the applied-security language for CT4104’s official cryptography and protocol outcomes.

Exam focus by part

  • CIA separates secrecy, tamper detection and availability.
  • authentication identifies, authorisation permits.
  • threat/vulnerability/control and residual risk differ.
  • cue: map property to control.

Question-demand diagnosis and answer plan

Name the asset and adversary; state the required property; select a control; explain its limit and a supporting control.

Question-type cues

  • Application cue: Design payroll-record protection for employees and contractors.
  • Analysis cue: A leaked API token exported records and audit events were altered.

Definitions, notation and discriminating comparisons

  • Confidentiality: prevent unauthorised reading.
  • Integrity: detect unauthorised change.
  • Authentication / authorisation: establish identity / decide permitted actions.
  • Threat, vulnerability, control: possible harm, weakness, safeguard.

Step-by-step methods and solution routes

  1. Identify asset, attacker and trust boundary.
  2. Separate secrecy, tamper detection, identity and permission.
  3. Map each to encryption, MAC/signature, login and access control.
  4. State a residual risk and monitoring or recovery control.

Reasoning checkpoints

  1. Use and justify: CIA separates secrecy, tamper detection and availability.
  2. Use and justify: authentication identifies, authorisation permits.
  3. Use and justify: threat/vulnerability/control and residual risk differ.
  4. Use and justify: cue: map property to control.

Worked examples and method extensions

A records portal needs private, unaltered requests. TLS protects traffic confidentiality and integrity; login authenticates a user; authorisation restricts records. Encryption alone does not decide whether Alice may read Bob’s record.

Exam-paper-led practice

Practice question 1 [medium/hard]

Scenario and demand: A payroll portal lets employees view payslips and contractors upload invoices. A leaked API token exported records and an attacker altered audit events. Map the distinct security properties to controls. [9 marks]

Question-demand diagnosis and fastest route: Separate the failures: confidentiality of payslips needs authenticated sessions, least-privilege authorisation and encrypted transport/storage; integrity needs signed or append-only audit records and input-controlled updates; availability needs backups, rate limits and recovery. Authentication identifies the caller; authorisation decides whether that caller may read a payslip. Rotate/revoke the leaked token, scope replacement tokens and investigate residual exposure. Trap: encryption alone cannot prevent an authorised-but-overprivileged token reading data.

Practice question 2 [medium/hard]

Scenario and demand: A manager says “we installed a firewall, so the risk is removed.” Use the portal to distinguish asset, threat, vulnerability, control and residual risk. [8 marks]

Question-demand diagnosis and fastest route: The payslip database is an asset; a criminal is a threat actor; an unrotated broadly scoped token is a vulnerability; token rotation and least privilege are controls. Risk combines likelihood and impact, not a synonym for the attacker. A firewall may reduce reachable paths but leaves phishing, credential theft and insider misuse; these are residual risks requiring monitoring and response. Trap: do not label a control itself as the threat.

Topic-specific traps and diagnosis

  • Calling encryption authentication.
  • Equating authentication with authorisation.
  • Claiming one control removes all risk.

Exam marking checklist

  • Asset and property named?
  • Mechanism and limit justified?
  • Layered control included?
